title: The Loop That Makes ATP Alone
endLine: Looping electrons around Photosystem I adds ATP without adding NADPH.

scenes.tts: Two light-driven lifts carry each electron from water to N A D P H. The protons left behind make A T P. But the Calvin cycle needs more A T P than that. How can a leaf make A T P alone?
scenes.narration: Two light-driven lifts carry each electron from water to NADPH. The protons left behind make ATP. But the Calvin cycle needs more ATP than that. How can a leaf make ATP alone?
scenes.caption: Two light-driven lifts carry each electron from water to NADPH. The protons left behind make ATP. But the Calvin cycle needs more ATP than that. How can a leaf make ATP alone?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's world and colour map with no reset: a wide schematic thylakoid cross-section filling about 70% of the frame height, stroma above a thick membrane band and lumen below, tiny lumen particles drifting throughout. COLOUR BY CONCEPT, as in the first film: electron bead GOLD; photon waves RED-GOLD; 'Photosystem II' block BLUE (left); 'cytochrome b6f' block TEAL (centre); 'Photosystem I' block GREEN (right of centre); 'ATP synthase' block GOLD (far right); NADP+/NADPH block GREEN in the stroma; H+ discs BLUE-edged when they come from water, TEAL-edged when they come from b6f. New in this film: the cyclic loop path is ORANGE. Recap motion on the first two sentences: two GOLD beads ride both lifts (photon at Photosystem II, downhill through b6f, photon at Photosystem I) and together turn the GREEN NADP+ block into NADPH; H+ discs gather in the lumen and leak through ATP synthase, which drops a small 'ATP' token into the stroma. On 'the Calvin cycle needs more', two upright bins rise in the upper-left stroma: a GOLD bin 'ATP' and a GREEN bin 'NADPH', each with a target line (GOLD at 3, GREEN at 2). The NADPH bin fills to its line; the ATP bin stalls visibly below its line (schematic). On the question, a large white question mark hangs over the stalled ATP bin and the text 'ATP alone?' appears across the top.

Title 'The Loop That Makes ATP Alone' fades in above the membrane for 2 s while the question text fades out. The two bins stay; lumen particles and a slow queue of dim GOLD beads keep moving along the linear route.

scenes.tts: Count per oxygen molecule released. Linear flow makes two N A D P H and leaves twelve protons in the lumen. The Calvin cycle spends three A T P for every two N A D P H.
scenes.narration: Count per oxygen molecule released. Linear flow makes 2 NADPH and leaves 12 protons in the lumen. The Calvin cycle spends 3 ATP for every 2 NADPH.
scenes.caption: Count per oxygen molecule released. Linear flow makes 2 NADPH and leaves 12 protons in the lumen. The Calvin cycle spends 3 ATP for every 2 NADPH.
scenes.visual: Same cross-section. Empty the bins and the lumen, then replay one O2's worth of linear flow: four GOLD beads, one after another, each lifted at Photosystem II and again at Photosystem I. A bubble labelled 'O2' leaves Photosystem II once. In the lumen an H+ counter fills to '12' as 4 BLUE-edged discs arrive from water and 8 TEAL-edged discs arrive at b6f (computed: 4 from water plus 2 per electron at b6f). The GREEN NADPH bin fills to '2', exactly at its line. On 'spends three A T P', the GOLD bin's target line at '3' brightens and a tag beside the bins reads 'Calvin cycle: 3 ATP : 2 NADPH'.

scenes.tts: Those protons pay at A T P synthase. Its rotor has fourteen subunits, each carrying one proton across per turn. One full turn makes three A T P. So fourteen protons buy three.
scenes.narration: Those protons pay at ATP synthase. Its rotor has 14 subunits, each carrying one proton across per turn. One full turn makes 3 ATP. So 14 protons buy 3.
scenes.caption: Those protons pay at ATP synthase. Its rotor has 14 subunits, each carrying one proton across per turn. One full turn makes 3 ATP. So 14 protons buy 3.
scenes.visual: Zoom gently toward the GOLD ATP synthase block on the right while keeping the membrane band and the bins in view. Its rotor is drawn as a schematic ring of 14 equal slots (no molecular structure), labelled '14 subunits'. On 'one proton across per turn', single H+ discs step from the lumen into slots one at a time and the ring turns one slot per disc. On 'one full turn', a ghost ring completes 360 degrees and three 'ATP' tokens pop out at even thirds of the turn into the stroma. Caption tag under the ring: '14 H+ = 3 ATP'. Return the ring to its start before the scene ends.

scenes.tts: Twelve protons turn the rotor only twelve fourteenths of the way. That makes about two point six A T P, roughly zero point four short. The gap rests on that fourteen-subunit rotor.
scenes.narration: Twelve protons turn the rotor only twelve fourteenths of the way. That makes about 2.6 ATP, roughly 0.4 short. The gap rests on that 14-subunit rotor.
scenes.caption: Twelve protons turn the rotor only twelve fourteenths of the way. That makes about 2.6 ATP, roughly 0.4 short. The gap rests on that 14-subunit rotor.
scenes.visual: The 12 lumen H+ discs from s02 feed the ring; it turns 12 of 14 slots (about 309 degrees, computed as 12/14 of 360) and stops with two EMPTY slots glowing. ATP tokens drop into the GOLD bin as the ring turns: the bin fills to 'about 2.6' (computed: 12 x 3/14 = 2.57), short of its line at 3; a small bracket from the fill to the line reads 'about 0.4 short'. On 'rests on that fourteen-subunit rotor', the '14 subunits' label pulses once.

scenes.tts: Closing the gap costs two more protons. Cytochrome B six F pumps two for every electron it passes. Predict: where could one electron go, to add protons but no N A D P H?
scenes.narration: Closing the gap costs two more protons. Cytochrome b6f pumps two for every electron it passes. Predict: where could one electron go, to add protons but no NADPH?
scenes.caption: Closing the gap costs two more protons. Cytochrome b6f pumps two for every electron it passes. Predict: where could one electron go, to add protons but no NADPH?
scenes.visual: The two empty rotor slots glow with a tag '2 H+ missing'. Pan back to the full cross-section. On 'pumps two for every electron', one GOLD bead drops through the TEAL b6f block and exactly two TEAL-edged H+ discs fall into the lumen. Then a single new GOLD bead sits on top of Photosystem I after its lift, at ferredoxin, with two faint arrows leaving it: one toward the GREEN NADP+ block (crossed out: 'no NADPH') and one blank arrow with a '?' beside it. Question card across the top, white: 'Where can it go?'
Predict pause. The question card 'Where can it go?' stays. The GOLD bead at ferredoxin bobs gently; the two rotor slots keep glowing; lumen particles drift. No other change.

scenes.tts: Back to cytochrome B six F. At ferredoxin, the electron turns around instead of reaching N A D P plus. It falls through B six F, which pumps its two protons. Then it returns to photosystem one, and a photon lifts it again.
scenes.narration: Back to cytochrome b6f. At ferredoxin, the electron turns around instead of reaching NADP+. It falls through b6f, which pumps its two protons. Then it returns to Photosystem I, and a photon lifts it again.
scenes.caption: Back to cytochrome b6f. At ferredoxin, the electron turns around instead of reaching NADP+. It falls through b6f, which pumps its two protons. Then it returns to Photosystem I, and a photon lifts it again.
scenes.visual: The question card dissolves. The blank arrow becomes a thick ORANGE path curving from ferredoxin (above Photosystem I) back left to the TEAL b6f block. The GOLD bead rides it; the GREEN NADP+ block stays unchanged. As the bead falls through b6f, two TEAL-edged H+ discs drop into the lumen. The ORANGE path continues from b6f back to Photosystem I, closing a loop; on 'a photon lifts it again', a RED-GOLD photon wave strikes Photosystem I and the bead climbs to ferredoxin once more. The BLUE Photosystem II block dims to 40% for the whole loop: no water is touched. The loop is labelled 'cyclic flow'.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea. A T P is paid in protons. N A D P H is paid in electrons that reach the end. So a loop that never reaches the end buys A T P alone.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea. ATP is paid in protons. NADPH is paid in electrons that reach the end. So a loop that never reaches the end buys ATP alone.
scenes.caption: Here is the idea. ATP is paid in protons. NADPH is paid in electrons that reach the end. So a loop that never reaches the end buys ATP alone.
scenes.visual: Two currencies, one picture. On 'paid in protons', H+ discs in the lumen stream through the ATP synthase ring and a GOLD arrow links them to the GOLD ATP bin. On 'electrons that reach the end', a linear-route GOLD bead reaches the GREEN block and a GREEN arrow links it to the NADPH bin. On 'a loop that never reaches the end', the ORANGE loop glows: its bead circles Photosystem I and b6f, H+ discs fall, the ATP bin ticks up, and the NADPH bin does not move. Label beside the loop: 'protons only'.

scenes.tts: The chloroplast mixes the two routes. About one electron per oxygen molecule goes round the loop. Its two protons bring the total to fourteen: three A T P. The price is about nine photons per oxygen, instead of eight.
scenes.narration: The chloroplast mixes the two routes. About one electron per oxygen molecule goes round the loop. Its two protons bring the total to 14: three ATP. The price is about 9 photons per oxygen, instead of 8.
scenes.caption: The chloroplast mixes the two routes. About one electron per oxygen molecule goes round the loop. Its two protons bring the total to 14: three ATP. The price is about 9 photons per oxygen, instead of 8.
scenes.visual: Run both routes together for one O2: four GOLD beads take the linear route while one GOLD bead circles the ORANGE loop once. The lumen H+ counter climbs from '12' to '14' as the loop's two TEAL-edged discs arrive. The rotor ring turns a full 360 degrees with all 14 slots filled; the GOLD bin reaches its line at '3' while the GREEN bin stays at '2'. A photon counter above the membrane steps 8 then 9 (computed: 4 electrons x 2 lifts + 1 loop lift), labelled 'about 9 photons'.

scenes.tts: Arnon showed that isolated chloroplasts make A T P both ways. The loop uses only the second lift, one photon per electron. Alongside other balancing routes, it brings the output to three to two.
scenes.narration: Arnon showed that isolated chloroplasts make ATP both ways. The loop uses only the second lift, one photon per electron. Alongside other balancing routes, it brings the output to 3 to 2.
scenes.caption: Arnon showed that isolated chloroplasts make ATP both ways. The loop uses only the second lift, one photon per electron. Alongside other balancing routes, it brings the output to 3 to 2.
scenes.visual: A small tag 'Arnon: two ways' appears at top left. The two routes light in turn: the linear route GOLD from Photosystem II to NADPH, tagged 'non-cyclic'; then the ORANGE loop, tagged 'cyclic'. On 'only the second lift', the dimmed Photosystem II stays dark while one photon wave strikes Photosystem I. On 'other balancing routes', a faint dashed WHITE arrow labelled 'other routes' touches the bins (schematic, no amount). The bins settle at their lines with a ratio tag '3 : 2'.

scenes.tts: So the answer to the opening question is a detour. Electrons that finish the climb make N A D P H. Electrons that circle only pump protons. The chloroplast sets its ratio partly by how many circle.
scenes.narration: So the answer to the opening question is a detour. Electrons that finish the climb make NADPH. Electrons that circle only pump protons. The chloroplast sets its ratio partly by how many circle.
scenes.caption: So the answer to the opening question is a detour. Electrons that finish the climb make NADPH. Electrons that circle only pump protons. The chloroplast sets its ratio partly by how many circle.
scenes.visual: Return to the opening framing: full cross-section with the two bins upper left, the white question mark from s00 reappearing over the ATP bin and then dissolving into the ORANGE loop. On 'finish the climb', a GOLD bead completes the linear route into the GREEN block; on 'circle', a GOLD bead circles the ORANGE loop and H+ discs drop. On 'how many circle', two or three more beads peel off into the loop while the rest continue linearly; both bins stay at their lines.

End card over the dimmed but still moving thylakoid world (GOLD beads on both routes, the ORANGE loop turning, lumen particles drifting). Hex above large white centred text: 'Looping electrons around Photosystem I adds ATP without adding NADPH.'
